source.author: stat
source.text: sic urget, et ultro vitantem aspectus etiam pudibundaque longe ora reducentem premit astridentibus hydris intentatque faces; deiectam in lumina pallam diva trahit magnoque fugit questura Tonanti.
source.text_original: ' sic urget, et ultro / vitantem aspectus etiam pudibundaque longe / ora reducentem premit astridentibus hydris / intentatque faces; deiectam in lumina pallam / diva trahit magnoque fugit questura Tonanti.
source.text_english: Thus she presses on, and, though he avoids her and even turns his bashful face far away, she still hounds him, setting her hissing snakes on him and brandishing torches; the goddess drags down the shawl that had fallen over his eyes and flees, about to complain to great Thunderer.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Tyrrheni tergore piscis Peleos in thalamos vehitur Thetis; aequora delphin corripit, illa sedet deiecta in lumina palla nec love maiorem nasci suspirat Achillen.
reuse.text_original: Tyrrheni tergore piscis / Peleos in thalamos vehitur Thetis; aequora delphin / corripit, illa sedet deiecta in lumina palla / nec love maiorem nasci suspirat Achillen.
reuse.text_english: Peleus is borne to the bridal chambers by Thetis, a Tyrrhenian fish, on its back; the dolphin speeds over the seas. She sits with her cloak fallen over her eyes and does not sigh that Achilles is born, greater than Jupiter.
